“It is going to be a tough second season, we know that, but we feel there is more to come from the existing group. It was difficult last season with a lot of players coming in later and having to relocate to the area and settle as the season started, but they were great for us and I feel there is more to come this season.”

Sports.title: ‘He’s back’: Zinedine Zidane named France head coach in long-awaited homecoming
Sports.content:
For Tuesday’s front page, L’Équipe simply went with “Il revient” – “He’s back” – echoing the newspaper’s 2005 headline when Zinedine Zidane came out of international retirement. At the time, the midfielder’s upcoming return was seen as a major boost to Les Bleus’ ailing World Cup qualifying campaign. There was a similar sense of anticipation now as the roads around the French Football Federation headquarters in Paris were closed off for Zidane’s unveiling as head coach. A crowd of France fans had gathered outside by the overground Métro tracks with flags, flares and drums, as more than a hundred journalists and TV cameras were ushered into the building.

The fact that Zidane would be next in line to lead France after Didier Deschamps had been an open secret for several years and by the end of the World Cup his arrival was all but confirmed. The new head coach entered the press conference room on Tuesday morning only minutes after his appointment was confirmed by the FFF’s executive committee, but the feeling in France was that the occasion was a couple of decades in the making.

“It’s a new cycle,” the FFF president, Philippe Diallo, said after a preamble in which he paid tribute to Deschamps’ 14-year tenure. Talks with the 1998 World Cup hero, Diallo said, began in February 2025, the month after Deschamps announced he would step down this summer. “Zinedine Zidane is one of the legends of French football and he had made it known that it was one of his dreams to manage the French national team,” Diallo said. “We wanted someone with the aura, the ability, and the hearts of our fans and the French people to manage what is one of the best national teams in the world.”

View image in fullscreen France supporters gather in Paris to celebrate the confirmation of one of the greatest players in Les Bleus’ history as their new head coach. Photograph: Teresa Suárez/EPA

For Zidane, this announcement was the culmination of nearly half a decade of waiting in the wings. “I had several offers from clubs in the last four to five years, but I turned them all down for France,” the former Real Madrid manager said. “The national team is the only thing I wanted. I’ve been with the French teams since I was a kid, all the way up to the senior team. I’m a bit emotional. You might not be able to tell, but I am incredibly excited.”

Zidane declared it was the greatest day of his managerial career. “It’s an immense joy. I am ready for the challenge.”

The five years that have passed since the end of Zidane’s second spell in Madrid will have been spent preparing to take over Les Bleus. “I’ve been watching France as a supporter, but also as a future manager. I don’t think there are any traps. It’s new to me, but I’m not scared. This is what I wanted.” The 54-year-old’s first public appearance as head coach was light on the details of his plans for the national team. He notably sidestepped a question about whether Kylian Mbappé would retain the armband, insisting that he would have to meet the team and its “extraordinary players” first of all. “We need to keep this team winning,” he said, adding that he was impressed with what he had seen during the World Cup.

“I was a No 10 in my playing days,” he said when asked about the style of play he would look to implement. Whether his answer implies a continuation of Deschamps’ attacking shift remains to be seen, but his answers did hint at some kind of change of direction. “Laurent [Blanc] was Laurent, Didier was Didier, and Zizou is Zizou,” he said playfully.

One of Zidane’s long-term objectives will be to compete with the reigning world champions, who have now beaten France in three consecutive tournament semi‑finals. “I spent 25 years in Spain and you know what that means,” he said, before pointing out that the task ahead went beyond beating La Roja. “I know Spanish football very well, but they won’t be the only opponents. You have to beat all of the teams.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Zinedine Zidane was sent off by Horazio Elizondo for butting Italy’s Marco Materazzi in the chest in the 2006 World Cup final. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Zidane’s four-year contract will begin next month, with his extended staff to be unveiled a few weeks before the first internationals of the new season. “We’ll see each other again in September to talk about it. It’s a good thing that we’ll have three weeks with the players.” The focus for now, Zidane said, is on his first match in charge, which will be in Turkey on 25 September.

His homecoming, meanwhile, will be against Italy, just over 20 years after his dramatic exit from the international stage. If the raucous reception as he stepped out of the FFF headquarters is anything to go by, it will be one of the more memorable evenings in the Stade de France’s history.

Sports.title: Roberto Mancini returns as Italy head coach with Claudio Ranieri named technical director
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini has agreed to be Italy head coach for a second time, the president of the Italian Football ​Federation (FIGC), Giovanni Malagò, said on Tuesday, also confirming Claudio Ranieri would take over as technical director.

Mancini replaces Gennaro Gattuso, who ⁠left the post in April after Italy failed to qualify for a third World Cup in succession, and returns to a job he held between 2018 and 2023. He led the national team to European Championship glory in 2021 with a penalty shootout victory over England at Wembley but then failed to reach the 2022 World Cup and a slow start to Euro 2024 qualifying. In total, Mancini managed Italy for 58 matches during his first spell and at club level has managed Inter, Fiorentina and Manchester City, where he spent three years and guided them to their first Premier League title in 2011-12.

“Mancini is the coach,” Malago ‌said on Tuesday. “I believed that the best person to become head coach was ‌Roberto Mancini.”

The former FIGC technical director ‌Paolo Maldini and his adviser, Leonardo, resigned from their roles on Monday after Andrea Pirlo’s appointment as head coach was blocked because of the former midfielder’s ties to a Russian betting firm. Pep Guardiola was the association’s first choice but turned down the job last month.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ranieri replaces ⁠Maldini. The 74-year-old, who led Leicester City to the Premier League title in ​2016, will oversee technical operations and ​elite football development across Italy’s national team structures. “I needed someone with ​whom I could share ‌the decision on ​the coach, because ​without that shared view my reasoning would have carried little weight,” Malago said. “So consequently, we have a new coach and a new technical director for Italy.”

Sports.title: Why Jordan Henderson is allowed to join Chelsea for free despite having another year on Brentford contract
Sports.content:
Why Jordan Henderson is allowed to join Chelsea for free despite having another year on Brentford contract

Jordan Henderson has emerged as a surprise target for Chelsea and an exit from Brentford looks set to happen this summer.

The England international midfielder only joined the Bees last season, but he could now be on his way out on a free deal.



3 Henderson played 32 times in the Premier League for Brentford last season Credit: Getty

But how is that the case, considering Henderson still has one year left on his contract at the Gtech Community Stadium?

Well, it all comes down to an informal understanding agreed to by the club regarding a move away if an opportunity came up.

And now Chelsea are interested, they could end up signing the former Liverpool captain without having to pay a fee...



Why is Henderson able to leave for free?

talkSPORT understands that Henderson can leave Brentford for free due to an agreement made with owner Matt Benham.

The gentleman's agreement allows him to depart before the end of his contract at the club, which will be up in 2027.



No official clause is in his deal, but the stance remains, with all parties from day one verbally agreeing to the free exit.

Benham and Brentford are expected to honour their promise to Henderson if the chance to leave arises.



Chelsea's approach could now provide that opportunity.

It's understood that Henderson is keen on the transfer to Stamford Bridge ahead of the new Premier League season.

Permission has been given for him to make the move.

3 Henderson has a gentleman's agreement with Brentford that allows him to leave for free Credit: Getty

Chelsea's shock transfers

Henderson becoming a target for Chelsea came out of nowhere on Monday, considering he is now 36 years old.

And with the Blues also pushing for Danny Welbeck, many fans across the country were left in shock at their new strategy.



Xabi Alonso appears to be looking for leadership and veteran players rather than bringing in their usual young signings.

Welbeck, aged 35, is expected to complete his move to Stamford Bridge from Brighton later this week.

Then Henderson could well be the next through the door, with Alonso surprising many with his latest business.

Speaking on the signing of Henderson, talkSPORT host and Chelsea fan Rory Jennings said: "I think what we need to do is bring in some standards for sure.



3 The veteran midfielder looks set for Chelsea, along with Danny Welbeck Credit: Getty

"I don't think Jordan Henderson is the right answer. I quite like Henderson. I don't necessarily rate him, but I quite like him.

"I think what he did for Liverpool was an integral part of their success. He was an integral part of everything that Jurgen Klopp built."

He added: "I'm not convinced that Jordan Henderson is the answer. I'm not convinced that he's ready to play at this level.



"The fact that we're linked with him is minorly troubling."

Sports.title: Jack Grealish must stay in the Premier League – teams need a maverick in their squad
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish must stay in the Premier League – teams need a maverick in their squad

Sean Dyche believes Jack Grealish should be staying in the Premier League if he ends up leaving Manchester City this summer.

The experienced manager believes a 'maverick' like Grealish is needed in a squad, amid links to a transfer away to Saudi Arabia.



3 Dyche is a fan of Grealish and players with his type of character on the pitch Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands that there is interest from the Saudi Pro League for the winger, who spent last season with Everton.

Al Hilal are an option for Grealish this summer, with the club pursuing another attacker, including his ex-Toffees teammate Illiman Ndiaye, having already signed Crysencio Summerville from West Ham.

Man City are keen on selling the 30-year-old on a permanent deal, as he is entering the final year of his contract at the Etihad Stadium.



But if he does leave, Dyche wants him to remain in the Premier League, admitting he is a fan of Grealish's 'arrogance'.

Appearing in the talkSPORT studio, the former Burnley, Nottingham Forest and Everton boss was asked by talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook as to whether modern-day managers distrust maverick players, with Grealish described as 'non-conformative'.



To which Dyche quipped: "I think there might have been a bit of distrust when he was coming out of Albert Schloss [bar] a few times!

"I think Pep [Guardiola] was going: 'No, that's not ideal.'"

Before Dyche then added: "No, I know what you mean, I quite like a bit of arrogance.



"Not arrogance, controlled arrogance, a bit of Maverick spirit, a bit of an edge to players - on and off the pitch.

"I don't think that's a problem, but if it doesn't fit with what the business side of it is… because at the end of the day, it's fine when it fits.

3 Grealish chipped in with eight goal contributions for Everton when on loan last season

"I don't think there's a problem, to be fair, with maverick players, but they have to fit and do the job.



"You can only be a maverick if you're doing the job.

"There are no mavericks who weren't doing the job who become mavericks of a club because they get them out.

"They go, 'No, if you're not doing the job, you're not doing the job.'

"But most teams need a maverick or two, they're the ones that make it click."

When pressed whether a change of scenery could be a good thing for maverick players, Dyche simply stated: "Sometimes taking a step backwards to go forwards can be the case."



3 New Man City boss Maresca has a good relationship with Grealish Credit: Getty

Maresca on Grealish's future

So, Dyche thinks a potential move could help get the best out of Grealish again heading into the new season.

But could he end up staying at Man City under new boss Enzo Maresca?

"At the moment, he's here. He's a Man City player," Maresca said on Friday when he was asked about the winger.

"I always said the same. In any club I join, I like to know if there are players that belong to the club. It's my duty to try to coach them.



"Jack is here. I have a good relationship with Jack since I left. Also, we keep in touch, and the reason why is because he has a big heart and he's a very good guy.

"So this is the reason why. And then we see what happens."

Sports.title: Liverpool line up first Bradley Barcola bid as Premier League winger eyed as dream alternative
Sports.content:
Liverpool line up first Bradley Barcola bid as Premier League winger eyed as dream alternative

Liverpool are set to place an opening bid for Bradley Barcola, talkSPORT understands.

Preliminary talks have already taken place, but suggestions that Barcola has already agreed terms are premature.



4 Liverpool are set to make a bid for PSG and France star Barcola Credit: Getty

Liverpool explored signing Barcola in 2025 when a price of around €85million (around £73m) was quoted.

A year on, and PSG's starting valuation is €170m (around £145m).

PSG sources argue Barcola is a back-to-back Champions League winner and should be worth more than Elliot Anderson (£116m) and Morgan Rogers (£117m).

But Liverpool will point to the fact Barcola only has two years left on his current deal and will not sign a new contract.



talkSPORT understands their initial valuation will be around £80m.

The Reds already made a similar bid for Real Madrid-bound Yan Diomande, consisting of £68m (€80m) and a further £17m (€20m) in add-ons.

Although Liverpool view adding Barcola as an ideal scenario, there are no plans to overpay, even in an inflated market.



There remains huge faith in Rio Ngumoha, while Cody Gakpo will either stay or, under the right circumstances, be sold at a premium. And Vitor Munoz has already arrived from Osasuna.

Barcola scored 11 goals in 29 Ligue 1 games for PSG last season, adding another two in the Champions League for the club.



Meanwhile, for France at the World Cup this summer, he played eight times for his country, scoring three and assisting one goal.

4 Liverpool's valuation of the French winger is expected to be around £80million Credit: AFP

4 Bournemouth and Brazil star Rayan is considered a dream alternative for Liverpool Credit: Getty

Liverpool's alternative options

Liverpool are still looking for a pacy and versatile winger and have other targets in mind in case Barcola's price fails to drop.



These include Köln forward Said El Mala and Lille star Matias Fernandez-Pardo.

Brighton's Yankuba Minteh has also been discussed, but talks are not active.

Bournemouth's Rayan is also considered a dream target.

But the Brazilian teenager's release clause, of over €100m (around £85m), doesn't kick in until 2027.

Meanwhile, Chelsea's Pedro Neto is not believed to be on the Reds' list of potential targets.



4 Iraola has admitted that Liverpool need to sign another winger this summer Credit: Getty

'We definitely need to sign a winger'

Liverpool's imminent bid for Barcola comes after new boss Andoni Iraola openly admitted he wants another wide man.

He told reporters on Sunday: "No, I think it’s difficult to say a number [of players the Reds could sign] when the market is open, and you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad.

"There are obvious situations that we know where we need to sign players. A winger, for example – we definitely need to sign a winger.



"But there are other situations that we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what’s the cost, how we also see the players we have.

"We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust but it is still not the ideal situation.

"So, it will depend on a lot of things."

Sports.title: Coventry smash club-record transfer as they sign in-demand Premier League player
Sports.content:
Coventry City have completed the signing of goalkeeper Carl Rushworth in a club-record £22.5million deal, talkSPORT understands.

Rushworth spent last season on loan at Coventry from Brighton, helping the Sky Blues get promoted to the Premier League.



3 Rushworth played a big role in Coventry's promotion Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Brighton had rejected a £20million bid from the newly-promoted side in June.

But the clubs have now finalised an agreement that will see the English goalkeeper join permanently. The £22.5m deal includes a sell-on and buy-back option for the Seagulls.

The 24-year-old starred for the Sky Blues as they stormed to the Championship title last season.



Rushworth played every league game for Frank Lampard's side, conceding just 45 goals and keeping 17 clean sheets.

New transfer record

The deal sees Coventry blow their current transfer record out of the water.



talkSPORT understands

They broke their record earlier this summer, with the £15.4m arrival of Aurele Amenda from Eintracht Frankfurt.

It also represents a coup for Coventry, with other Premier League sides monitoring Rushworth earlier this summer.



The goalkeeper only had one year left on his deal, and he has been watched by England on multiple occasions.

Coventry's record signings Aurele Amenda (Frankfurt) - £15.4m - 2026 Haji Wright (Antalyaspor) - £7.7m - 2023 Craig Bellamy (Norwich) - £6.5m - 2000 Robbie Keane (Wolves) - £6m - 1999 Jack Rudoni (Huddersfield) - £5m - 2024

Huge fan

After playing every minute in the Championship, Lampard made it clear that he is a huge Rushworth fan.

Speaking about the goalkeeper last campaign, he said that England caps were waiting for him.

3 Coventry made another move for Rushworth after having a bid turned down Credit: Getty



He said: "Yes, for sure [he could play for his country]. I mean, without telling any England manager what to do…

"I know Jordan Pickford, who I worked with (at Everton), and is an incredible goalkeeper, and the goalkeepers are around him.

"But Rushy, just to isolate him, he’s got absolutely the talent to be able to play for his country, in my opinion.

"He just needs to keep working, but the levels he’s playing at are really, really good, and he’s been a big signing for us."



Coventry's transfer plans

talkSPORT also reported in June that Coventry had been weighing up a move for Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

The Southampton captain missed out on the chance at promotion to the top-flight due to the Saints sending an intern to spy on Middlesbrough ahead of the play-off semi-final first leg.

3 Lampard will lead Coventry into the Premier League for the first time in 25 years Credit: Getty

They have since signed defender Amenda from Frankfurt too.

But there is plenty more business expected to be made by Lampard, who, speaking on The Sports Bar with Jason Cundy and Jamie O'Hara after winning promotion, admitted there was lots to do.



The Chelsea legend said in May: "We've got a lot of work to do. We'll do it quickly, and I think I feel like we have to do it quickly.

"It's the owner's choice, a lot of these things, because he's the boss man in the football club. But the conversations obviously have to happen quickly, but also enjoy this little moment."

Sports.title: Footballer dragged out of car by armed gang in terrifying robbery as club gives statement
Sports.content:
Footballer dragged out of car by armed gang in terrifying robbery as club gives statement

Police have made an arrest after a Union Saint-Gilloise footballer was the victim of a violent robbery last weekend.

Footage posted on social media shows striker Mohammed Fuseini being attacked on the streets of Brussels on Sunday morning.



2 Fuseini was attacked by robbers in a terrifying ordeal on Sunday Credit: Getty

Fuseini was dragged out of his car by masked individuals and held in a headlock during the terrifying scenes.

Belgian outlet Het Laatste Nieuws (HLN) say the 24-year-old had his Rolex, worth between €8,000 and €14,000, stolen in the incident.

The attackers then fled the scene, with one of Fuseini's teammates said to have captured the attack on film.



It is said to have taken place close to the exit of Bloody Louis, which is a nightclub in central Brussels.

Union SG released a statement on Fuseini's condition which, via HLN, said: "The images from last Sunday are particularly harrowing.



"He subsequently went to the hospital for a check-up and received excellent care there from the Brussels police, whom we sincerely thank for their outstanding work.

"The injuries are not serious, and he resumed training yesterday."

"Three people were the victims of a robbery with violence as they made their way to their vehicle in Brussels," the public prosecutors office said.



"According to the initial findings of the investigation, several people allegedly attacked them and took various valuable items, including watches, telephones, and personal belongings."

A 23-year-old suspect has been arrested, with the office adding: "During a search of his home, items reported stolen were recovered.

"The Brussels Public Prosecutor's Office requested an investigating judge and asked for the suspect's detention.

"The suspect was charged with theft with violence committed by a gang and placed under an arrest warrant."



Following their arrest, the suspect is being held in Haren prison and his lawyer did not confirm if the watches were located at his home.

"I do not want to say anything more about that, because the judicial investigation is still ongoing," Samuel Rosenblatt said.

"My client is aware of the seriousness of the facts and regrets them," he added.

Fuseini joined Union SG in 2024 from Austrian side SK Sturm Graz.

2 Fuseini is said to have had his watch stolen during the attack Credit: Getty



He has scored 14 goals in 71 appearances for the club, with whom he has won the Belgian Pro League and Belgian Cup.

The forward has made two Champions League appearances at Union SG against Bayern Munich and Atalanta.

Fuseini also faced Scottish giants Rangers during the 2024/25 Europa League league phase.

He has made two appearances for Ghana and scored one goal in a 4-0 friendly win over Trinidad and Tobago last year.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s hopes of signing Vinicius Jr fade as Real Madrid step up contract talks
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s hopes of signing Vinicius Jr fade as Real Madrid step up contract talks

Jose Mourinho wants Vinicius Junior to stay at Real Madrid, who are working on talks to extend his contract, talkSPORT understands.

Real are determined not to lose their superstar on a free and they hope he'll sign a new deal, with progress being made this week.



3 Real Madrid are hopeful that Vini Jr will sign a new contract rather than leave Credit: Getty

Arsenal only ever explored the idea of signing the Brazilian internally and always knew the Spanish giants wanted to keep him.

It means the Gunners' hopes of signing Vinicius Jr. appear to be slipping following their initial interest in the winger.

The Premier League champions had contemplated making a move, but he was only a transfer option and not a key target.



talkSPORT reported on Monday that they have the finances available to make Vini Jr. their highest-paid player and they were prepared to open talks if they were given any encouragement from him.

Reports claim the 26-year-old Brazilian has been seeking as much as €550,000 (£470,000) on his next contract.



That would see him overtake Bukayo Saka as Arsenal's highest earner by a massive margin, with the England international earning £300,000 a week.

However, with Mourinho wanting to keep Vini Jr. at Real Madrid, his move to North London is looking unlikely.



He was also offered to Liverpool, but they opted not to pursue him - and he could now sign a new deal at Real soon.

If Vini Jr stays in Spain, he will be part of a squad that includes multiple new faces signed by Mourinho this summer.

Yan Diomande is set to join from RB Leipzig, following Bernardo Silva, Marc Cucurella, Ibrahima Konate and Denzel Dumfries through the door at the Bernabeu.

3 Mourinho wants to keep his Brazilian superstar at the club this summer Credit: Getty



3 It means Arsenal are set to miss out on another big name they were interested in Credit: Getty

Missing out on another star

Arsenal have been hoping to bring in a star forward this summer, but they are now set to miss out on another target.

If Vinicius Jr. doesn't make the move and stays at Real Madrid, the Gunners will have failed to sign him or Morgan Rogers.

Mikel Arteta had been eyeing Rogers and the club were understood to be preparing a bid for the England international.



However, London rivals Chelsea swooped in to sign him for a record-breaking £117million last week.

It leaves Arsenal still searching for a big-money arrival, with a move for Vini Jr. now not expected to materialise.

The Gunners have already signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge as a replacement for Leandro Trossard, who joined Besiktas.

They have also brought in goalkeeper Illan Meslier on a free transfer and signed Piero Hincapie on a permanent deal.

Sports.title: Stadium still a building site just weeks before it’s due to host European game
Sports.content:
Stadium still a building site just weeks before it’s due to host European game

Getafe face a race against time to get their stadium ready to host European matches, with major reconstruction works still incomplete.

The Spanish side are set to take part in the Conference League play-offs in a matter of weeks, having qualified after finishing seventh in LaLiga last season.

3 Entire stands at the Estadio Coliseum look largely incomplete, with just weeks until Getafe's Conference League opener Credit: Instagram / getafecf

But with their two-legged European showdown set to take place in late August, their Estadio Coliseum home still looks a way off being fit to host games.

Getafe have been playing their home games at a reduced capacity since redevelopment works on the ground started in June last year.

Their revamp has stepped up over the summer, as club bosses look to increase the venue by 2,000 seats to a 18,500 capacity, and with a roof covering every stand

The project isn't due to be complete for another 18 months, meaning it won't be ready by the start of the new season.

However, construction chiefs now have a new deadline to meet, as they are now scrambling to ensure the stadium will meet UEFA regulations in time for Getafe's Conference League clash.

European football‘s governing body sets out regulations on floodlighting, media infrastructure, hospitality areas and various other facilities for a venue to be allowed to host UEFA-sanctioned matches.

And the Estadio Coliseum could struggle to satisfy all of their demands in the coming weeks, if footage shared online is anything to go by.

Work to be done

In a recent video shared on Getafe's official social media pages, construction work looks to be far from complete.

With the stadium still resembling a building site, the stand behind one of their goals only appears to have seating in its lower tier.

Further footage shows another stand being rebuilt, with cranes visible from above as the work remains ongoing.

3 Footage has shown Getafe’s home ground is still in the midst of major reconstruction works Credit: Instagram / getafecf

The exterior of the ground is also in the midst of reconstruction, with the outside of the stands being rebuilt surrounded by rubble.

Building equipment and trucks can be seen around the ground, while the video also shows construction staff continuing their work on the renovation project.

Solution snubbed

Getafe had been in touch with city rivals Atletico Madrid about the prospect of playing European home games at the Metropolitano, located roughly 16 miles from the Estadio Coliseum.

But they have instead decided to pursue their current project, and will look to get their home ground ready in time.

The next part of the stadium plans involve the demolition of the Tribuna Stand, which runs along the west side of the pitch.

This will put the two-tiered grandstand out of action for the start of the new season, while the North Stand will also be out of use until the end of the year as work remains ongoing.

3 The Estadio Coliseum will soon have its capacity increased to 18,500 seats Credit: Getty

However, the South and Lateral Stands are expected to be completed in time.

Founded in 1983, Getafe moved into the Estadio Coliseum 15 years later in 1998.

With Spanish giants Real Madrid and Atletico the city's dominant teams, Getafe's home ground is the third-biggest of Madrid's three LaLiga teams.

Real's Santiago Bernabeu comes out on top, boasting a 83,186 capacity, ahead of the Metropolitano Stadium, with Atleti's home able to host 70,000 spectators.

However, Getafe's ground does trump Rayo Vallecano, whose Vallecas Stadium has a capacity of 14,708.

And while the Estadio Coliseum faces a race to be fit for European football, Rayo have concerns of their own and will be redeveloping their ground after serious safety concerns were detected.

Sports.title: Europe could boycott World Cup as UEFA consider bid to defeat Gianni Infantino after controversial plans
Sports.content:
Europe could boycott World Cup as UEFA consider bid to defeat Gianni Infantino after controversial plans

European nations could BOYCOTT future World Cups if FIFA president Gianni Infantino sells parts of FIFA to private investors.

It emerged on Tuesday that Infantino is looking to sell World Cup stakes to private investors in a controversial move that could earn him millions.



4 Infantino is reportedly planning to sell World Cup stakes Credit: AFP

This would lead to the introduction of a new company that will be in charge of top competitions across men's and women's football.

The World Cup and Club World Cup would also come under control, and therefore expansion or more regular editions could materialise.

In addition, the plan is said to have been discussed with figures close to US president Donald Trump.



Joshua Kushner, whose brother Jared is Trump's son-in-law, has been eyed as the primary investor candidate with the bank JP Morgan.

The plan would also see stakes worth around $20million (£15m) given to all of the 211 member associations involved with FIFA.



Once his last term as president concludes, which could be in 2031 at the earliest, Infantino would likely be the group's commissioner.

World Cup cancelled?

It's sparked fury in UEFA with European football's governing body considering taking drastic action to prevent this from happening.



talkSPORT understands European nations will discuss this in an emergency meeting this week to figure out the next steps.

Meanwhile, there is growing support for UEFA to find a candidate to stand against Infantino at the next FIFA elections, which take place in Morocco on November 18.

Infantino has been in the role since 2016, the Switzerland-born 56-year-old replacing the disgraced Sepp Blatter.

4 UEFA are set to launch a fightback against Infantino's controversial move Credit: AFP



UEFA hit back at FIFA plans

Following the publication of The Times' article, UEFA released a statement to condemn the plan, which read: "This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross.

"UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

"The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially.

"None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell."

Infantino under the spotlight

The 2026 World Cup was yet another spectacle on the pitch, but a series of controversies off it overshadowed the tournament.



Infantino has been the subject of intense scrutiny for his relationship with Trump, even before the World Cup began.

4 Infantino and his relationship with Trump has been a hot topic Credit: Getty

Trump was awarded the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize during the group stage draw in December.

He was championed by the FIFA president for 'unwavering commitment' to world peace through 'notable leadership and action'.



During the 2026 World Cup, United States striker Folarin Balogun had his one-match ban for a red card suspended for a year.

talkSPORT revealed that Trump called Infantino to review the decision, the only one of its kind out of all the 15 red card decisions.

In response, The Norwegian FA have intended to make a formal complaint to FIFA's ethics committee over Trump's intervention.

The red card has also been linked with potential betting irregularities.



4 The report has sparked more conflict between FIFA and UEFA Credit: Getty

On Monday, it was reported that a US lawmaker has requested for Infantino to appear before the House Judiciary Committee.

Rep. Jamie Raskin wants Infantino's relationship with Trump to be scrutinised and FIFA to provide all records of their contact with the politician.

Infantino has responded to the criticism aimed at him by accusing people of 'spreading hate'.



He called upon critics to instead 'reflect, meditate, pray, or watch a football match'.

FIFA pump in more money

A matter of hours after UEFA's statement, FIFA announced plans to give $10billion of funding on football development, subject to approval by FIFA member assocations.

Global football's governing body says this would be part of the newly-launched FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which is a "new FIFA-owned and controlled subsidiary consolidating FIFA’s commercial and event operations."

FIFA Forward Enterprise is controlled by FIFA, as is exclusive authority over football governance, competitions, match calendar, and all regulatory and sporting decisions.



It says the enterprise would raise up to $4.2bn later this year to fund the wider FIFA Fast Forward Programme "based on an initial equity valuation of $20bn by carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests in FFE."

FIFA claims all net benefits will be reinvested back into football worldwide.

Sports.title: Silver lining for England's 'sexy and aggressive' track Goddess: Amy Hunt misses out on Commonwealth Games gold in women's 100m final
Sports.content:
Silver lining for England's 'sexy and aggressive' track Goddess: Amy Hunt misses out on Commonwealth Games gold in women's 100m final

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

As Amy Hunt paraded through the interview room, a beaming smile and the English flag draped over her drenched shoulders, she wiggled her fingers to flash her silver rings.

‘I need to start wearing gold jewellery,’ she laughed, having just finished second in the 100 metres final. There was no shame whatsoever in her silver medal, but Hunt has always been one of life’s over achievers.

‘If anyone wants to buy some gold rings for me, that would be amazing!’ added the Cambridge University graduate.

She lost three of her acrylic nails on the starting blocks. The conditions in Glasgow were filthy, splashing and dashing through torrential rain to finish in a time of 10.98 seconds.

‘It was pretty gross on the start line,’ she said. ‘My fingers were underwater but you just have to roll with the punches at champs.’

Throughout the evening, stadium staff pushed giant squeegee machines over the surface to soak up the water. They absorb 60 litres per minute but nothing could prevent the track from turning into a 100m slip and slide.

Amy Hunt sprinted to silver in the women's 100m final at the Commonwealth Games

New Zealand's Zoe Hobbs made a fast start to the final and held off Hunt to claim the gold

Hunt, seen congratulating Hobbs, has view this all as part of her long-term project building towards the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games

Billy Connolly was born 15 minutes away this stadium, which is usually occupied by the Glasgow Warriors rugby team. As the city’s windswept comedian once said: ‘There are two seasons in Scotland: June and winter.’

Outside of Scotstoun, volunteers were determined not to be brought down by the washout. ‘No Scotland, no party,’ they chanted. In the uncovered stand behind the finish line, most of the party had left for shelter by the time Hunt crossed the line.

For Hunt, you suspect this is all part of a long-term project to put her in medal contention for the 200m at the 2028 Olympics. The 24-year-old has been working hard to improve her start - and it was her top-end speed pulled her back into the medal positions. So far in 2026, Hunt has set personal bests over 50, 60 and 100 metres. It will all help improve her chances the warmer climates of Los Angeles.

Here, however, it Zoe Hobbs of New Zealand won gold, surprising the field from Lane 7.

‘I had a really terrible first 60 metres,’ said Hunt. ‘So I think it just shows the calibre of my top end speed that I could dig myself out of the horrendous ditch that I dug in the first half of the race.

‘It was the first 10 for me. I'm a legitimate starter. I can get it right, and today I got it really badly wrong. My top end speed is so formidable that I was able to claw back that silver but I think gold was definitely there for the taking. I beat Zoe in the semis - and she's an incredible athlete. She ran a PB to win, but I think gold was definitely there.’

Heather Oakes was the last woman to win 100m gold for England in the Commonwealths. That was back in 1986, when 32 nations boycotted the competition because Margaret Thatcher refused to impose sanctions on South Africa's apartheid government. The wait goes on.

Many of the world’s fastest women stayed away from Glasgow this week. Olympic champion Julien Alfred, of St Lucia, was among the absentees, along with the British Virgin Islands’ Adaejah Hodge, who has clocked the fastest time in the world this year. You suspect they were not full of regret when they turned on their TV sets to see athletes huddled under umbrellas. The high jump was delayed for almost two hours.

Englishman Elliot Jones raced earlier in the evening, losing out in his 100m semi-final. The 28-year-old needed to wring out his running spikes as he headed back into the changing room. ‘There was water all over the lane,’ said Jones, who watched Cameroonian Emmanuel Eseme win the final with a Games record time of 9.83s.

‘It felt like I couldn't get any traction. I didn't feel like I was moving anywhere. It's frustrating, but everyone's got the same conditions. I got in the blocks and I was pushing water out my lanes. In between the false start and the start, the water had repoured. It's a Scottish summer, isn't it?’

This was a summer headline that Hunt was not prepared to miss out on. Her parents travelled up from Newark to watch, booking an Airbnb with her coach. Only the Commonwealths? Tell that to her mentor, the double gold medallist Darren Campbell.

‘I think it's really, really important as a track athlete,’ said Hunt, who won 200m silver in the World Championships in Tokyo last September. ‘We don't get much representation in terms of media. We're not NBA players. We're not on TV three times a week, when everyone's seeing our faces.

‘It's really, really important in terms of my journey as an athlete, my legacy is an athlete. I don't want to go on my Wikipedia page in 30 years' time and just see one or two medals. I want to see lists and lists of medals. This is my first Commonwealth Games, so it was really good to come here.’

And the Glaswegian storm clouds, at least, had a silver lining.

Sports.title: UEFA lay into FIFA over 'proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup' in a move that could 'make president Gianni Infantino millions' - as plan is labelled a 'nuclear bomb' for football
Sports.content:
UEFA have hit out at a leaked FIFA plan to sell stakes in the World Cup in a move that could make its president Gianni Infantino millions.

News broke in The Times on Tuesday afternoon that FIFA boss Infantino was considering selling parts of the tournament to private investors and forming a new company in a deal that could be worth around £15billion.

The report added that Infantino could become the commissioner of that company once his role at FIFA ends in 2031, a highly lucrative position that estimates suggest could pay him more than $50million-a-year.

The bank JPMorgan is said to be handling the process and the Donald Trump administration is understood to have been consulted.

The proposal has already received widespread criticism from across football, with one source telling The Times it would be a 'nuclear bomb' for the sport and another arguing it would 'potentially be much worse than the European Super League'.

It is understood the English FA were completely unaware of the proposal.

And UEFA, which has been critical of FIFA and Infantino's actions in recent times, hit out at the plans.

FIFA are reportedly planning to sell stakes in the World Cup in a hugely contentious move

UEFA launched a strongly worded statement slamming plans that 'crossed a line' (pictured - UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin)

'This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross,' they said in a statement. 'UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association.

'So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

'The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.'

Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter also condemned the governing body's reported plan.

'The close relationship between the FIFA President and the US President has reached a financial dimension that is deeply damaging football,' Blatter wrote on X.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham also hit out at FIFA on social media, writing: 'No one has the right to sell our game.'

'Let me say this very directly. Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

'The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell.

'Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.'

If the move was to go ahead, the global football calendar would likely be affected.

For example, the Men's and Women's World Cup may be expanded or held more regularly than every four years, while the Club World Cup could face similar changes.

Joshua Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, was reported to be one of the potential investors

As part of the proposal, all 211 member associations would have stakes that would make up 20 per cent of the total company and be worth around $20million (£15million) each.

That is a larger figure than many of their annual revenues, and they would be given the option to sell them to raise funds.

FIFA would retain a majority stake in the new entity and private investors would be able to take on minority stakes.

FIFA are a not-for-profit organisation and enjoy tax-free status at their HQ in Switzerland.

For the most recent cycle of 2022-2026, their revenue is expected to be around $15billion (£11.3billion) – much of which came from this summer's World Cup – meaning this would provide a lucrative opportunity for individuals to be involved in.

The Times added that the blueprint for the potential selling of stakes has been discussed among senior FIFA figures and potential investors, which could include Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared – and they have signed non-disclosure agreements.

Some of those potential investors are understood to have even spoken internally about 'buying FIFA'.

Infantino's proposed new role could be extremely lucrative. Figures close to the plan are said to see it on a par with the NFL, whose commissioner Roger Goodell earns about $64million a year.

The reports come at a time when Infantino is already under fire for a variety of reasons following the World Cup.

This includes the US visa restrictions that affected supporters and officials from many countries, the extremely high prices of tickets and Infantino's links with Trump, which came to a head after Folarin Balogun's red card was suspended following a phone call by the US President to the Swiss administrator.

When contacted for comment, FIFA confirmed plans to launch a new body called FIFA Forward Enterprise, which they described as a 'controlled subsidiary consolidating FIFA's commercial and event operations'.

They added that 'FIFA would retain sole control of FFE and exclusive authority over football governance, competitions, match calendar, and all regulatory and sporting decisions,' and claimed the move would increase the funding available to all 211 member associations.

The Daily Mail Sport also contacted the White House for comment.

Sports.title: Man City's forgotten man Kalvin Phillips is set for ANOTHER loan move after being left out of Man City squad for Asia tour - with injured Jack Grealish also absent
Sports.content:
Man City's forgotten man Kalvin Phillips is set for ANOTHER loan move after being left out of Man City squad for Asia tour - with injured Jack Grealish also absent

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Kalvin Phillips is finalising a new loan move to Sheffield United after being left off Manchester City's squad list to tour Asia.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed last month, Chris Wilder is keen to re-sign the 30-year-old, who has two years left on his contract, despite a difficult loan spell last season.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday.

Phillips has endured a torrid time since joining City for £42 million from Leeds United and is keen to kickstart his career.

The 30-year-old former England international was desperate to make an impact, but his lack of games in recent seasons and subsequent shortage of match sharpness put him at a physical disadvantage.

The 31-cap international previously had loan spells with West Ham and Ipswich in the Premier League before linking up with Sheffield United in January.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday

View this post on Instagram

Including his loan moves, he has made a total of 46 league appearances since joining City almost four years ago.

Talking to BBC Radio Sheffield towards the end of the season, Wilder said: 'He'll have a lot of people still after him. We've brought a really good pro in. He was unlucky with his injury and he's not played as much as he wanted to play.

MAN CITY TOUR SQUAD Goalkeepers Gianluigi Donnarumma, Marcus Bettinelli, Max Chabot, Jack Wint. Defenders Rayan Ait-Nouri, Max Alleyne, Kaden Braithwaite, Josko Gvardiol, Matty Henderson-Hall, Abdukodir Khusanov, Rico Lewis, Stephen Mfuni, Vitor Reis. Midfielders Claudio Echeverri, Phil Foden, Jaden Heskey, Mateo Kovacic, Jeremy Monga, Divine Mukasa, Nico Gonzalez, Xavier Parker, Tijjani Reijnders, Floyd Samba, Antoine Semenyo, Savinho. Forwards Mahamadou Sangare, Divin Mubama, Ryan McAidoo.

'I spoke to him and said we'd love to be an option for you, your agent and your parent club if that is a possibility.

'He certainly ticks the box in terms of personality and characteristics, off the pitch and on it. If there's an opportunity I'm sure we'll try and explore that one.'

Jack Grealish has also been left out of City's pre-season tour as he continues his rehabilitation and individual training programme.

Grealish joined Everton on loan at the beginning of last season and his time with the Toffees got off to the perfect start as he notched two goals and six assists during the early months of the season.

But in January the attacker suffered a stress fracture during a game against his former club Aston Villa, which required surgery.

The injury marked the end of Grealish's season – and thereby killed his World Cup hopes - and he stayed at the Hill Dickinson club until the end of the season to undergo his rehabilitation.

He has since returned to City, posting a picture of himself on the grass last week with the caption: 'Nice to see everyone, am nearly there! Hopefully not long now till back training for good'.

There has been interest from Saudi Arabia - and Everton are also aware of his situation - but a decision on his future looks likely to come later in the window.

Savinho also wants to push through his move to Tottenham but City maintain his valuation has not been met and would want a replacement before they allow the 22-year-old to leave.

Sources at Tottenham indicate City's valuation has changed since initial talks.

City have considered the likes of Ibrahim Mbaye from PSG and Chelsea's Pedro Neto as potential wing additions.

Sports.title: Man United open to offers for FOUR academy graduates, Newcastle insist Arsenal have not made approach for Bruno Guimaraes, Nottingham Forest among list of clubs targeting Chelsea's Liam Delap: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Sky Blues near club-record £22.5m deal for Rushworth

Coventry City are closing on a £22.5million deal for Brighton goalkeeper Carl Rushworth.

Add ons will take the fee closer to £30m and a sell-on percentage will also be included.

A medical is being scheduled for later this week for the 25-year-old who also attracted interest from Newcastle United.

Coventry City are closing on a £22.5m deal for 25-year-old Brighton goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, who also attracted interest from Newcastle United

Bees line up Henderson replacement

Brentford are advancing in talks to sign Lens midfielder Mamadou Sangare as a potential replacement for Jordan Henderson.

The Bees have been talking to Lens for a couple of months about the Mali international in a deal that could be worth £40million, though they have faced competition from Crystal Palace who are managed by Sangare's former coach Pierre Sage.

The 24-year-old is keen on the move to the Premier League and Brentford hope to finalise terms ahead of their London rivals, with Henderson due to join Chelsea on a free transfer.

Brentford want two midfielders and are also weighing up a move for Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr.

They remain in talks over 18-year-old Ousmane Diabete from Genclirbirligi, amid competition from Spurs, but the teenager is regarded as one for the future.

Sarr, 23, has had interest from Turkey but would be open to remaining in London if, as it seems, his first-team starting chances will be limited following Spurs' purchase of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes.

Brentford want two midfielders and are also weighing up a move for Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr

Fulham's Palacios talks continue

Fulham have held further talks over a deal for Real Madrid midfielder Cesar Palacios.

The 21-year-old made his debut for the senior team in January and is well known to Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa, who is keen to bring the Spain Under 20 international and forward Gonzalo Garcia to London from his former club.

Arokodare passes Ajax medical

Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare has passed his medical with Ajax.

The 25-year-old has also completed the paperwork on his loan with Ajax having the option to buy Arokodare for £17m.

The Dutch club will pay a £1m loan fee, with add-ons, if they reach the league phase of a European competition.

The 25-year-old has also completed the paperwork on his loan with Ajax having the option to buy Arokodare for £17m

United youngsters attracting attention

Manchester United are open to offers for Harry Amass, Dan Gore, Toby Collyer and Radek Vitek.

Several clubs have already made enquiries for goalkeeper Vitek and left-back Amass for loans and permanent deals while Gore and Collyer could also go on loan.

They will continue to train with the first team until other members of the squad re-join following their break for the World Cup.

However, their regular game time after that is more likely to come with the club's U21s so United are looking for them to gain more competitive action elsewhere.

Several clubs have already made enquiries for goalkeeper Vitek and left-back Amass (left) for loans and permanent deals

Stones set for Inter medical

Inter Milan are expecting John Stones to undergo a medical on Thursday is ahead of his move to Italy.

The England international and his representatives are finalising terms over a free transfer and a two-year deal.

The 32-year-old is a free agent after leaving Manchester City and Inter are progressing in talks for Christian Romero from Spurs also.

Meanwhile, Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile and West Ham's Jean-Clair Todibo are on Napoli's list as the Serie A side work on signing a new centre back.

John Stones is set for a medical at Inter Milan as he prepares to join on a free transfer

Phillips edges closer to Blades return

Kalvin Phillips is finalising a new loan move to Sheffield United after being left off Manchester City’s squad list to tour Asia.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed last month, Chris Wilder is keen to re-sign the 30-year-old - who has two years left on his contract - despite a difficult loan spell last season.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday.

Phillips has endured a torrid time since joining City for £42million from Leeds United and is keen to kickstart his career.

Manchester City's Kalvin Phillips is on the verge of re-joining Championship Sheffield United

Black Cats zero in on Methalie

Sunderland are continuing talks over a potential £26million deal for left-back Dayann Methalie from Toulouse.

As Daily Mail Sport previously reported, the France Under 21 international defender, who can also operate as a centre-back, emerged as a Sunderland target after previously attracting interest from Newcastle United.

But Regis Le Bris is hopeful Sunderland can bring him in on a five-year contract for what would be a record sale for Toulouse.

Dayann Methalie (right) emerged as a Sunderland target after previously attracting interest from Newcastle

Forest putting out feelers for Famalicao's Sa

Nottingham Forest are in talks to sign Portuguese attacking midfielder Gustavo Sa from Famalicao.

The 21-year-old was a target for Saudi Arabian clubs earlier in the year and West Ham this summer but Forest may now sign him and then send on loan to Olympiacos.

Sa was the captain of Famalicao last season, scoring four goals and claiming two assists from 34 appearances.

Tomiyasu training with Palace

Former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu is training with Crystal Palace after the expiry of his contract at Ajax.

The Japan international was expected to extend his contract but is a free agent after making just nine appearances since moving to Amsterdam on a short-term deal in January owing in part to a hamstring injury.

The 27-year-old is training with Palace in Como as part of the club’s pre-season preparations and could feature in a friendly this week. He has had interest from Venezia and Sassuolu, too.

Palace are playing in the Como Cup. They face Lens, new manager Pierre Sage's former side, tonight then take on Famalicao in two 45-minute games.

Takehiro Tomiyasu

Bees eye Sarr signing

Brentford are weighing up a move for Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr.

The Bees were looking to strengthen their options even before news of Jordan Henderson's proposed departure for Chelsea.

They remain in talks over 18-year-old Ousmane Diabate from Genclirbirligi, amid competition from Spurs, but the teenager is regarded as one for the future. They now want two more for the first team squad with Henderson heading towards Stamford Bridge.

Sarr, 23, has had interest from Turkey but would be open to remaining in London if, as it seems, his first team starting chances will be limited following Spurs' purchase of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes.

Pape Matar Sarr is on Brentford's radar, with Jordan Henderson wanted by Chelsea

Newcastle still waiting on Arsenal bid for Bruno

Newcastle United insist they have still to receive a formal approach from Arsenal for midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal have been preparing to make an official £70m-plus move for the Brazilian who is keen to join them but, so far, Newcastle sources say any proposals have come via the player's agent.

Newcastle manager Eddie Howe said at the weekend he was unsure what would happen over the 28-year-old's future.

Bruno Guimaraes wants to move to Arsenal but Newcastle say they are still waiting for a bid

Delap in demand with Chelsea set to sign Welbeck

Nottingham Forest remain among the list of clubs showing interest in Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

Danny Welbeck's pending arrival from Brighton is likely to leave fewer opportunities for 22-year-old Delap and clubs are enquiring to ascertain the deal required to sign the former Ipswich Town forward.

Forest, Everton and Newcastle United are just some of the clubs who have expressed interest in the former England U21 international.

Meanwhile, Forest have made an offer for Union Saint-Gilloise full-back Anan Khalaili as talks for Feyenoord's Givairo Read also continue.

Both players are also appreciated by Bournemouth and Newcastle United.

Liam Delap is a target for several clubs with his chances at Chelsea likely to be limited

Jorgensen leaves camp for France

Chelsea goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen has left their camp in Australia ahead of joining sister club Strasbourg.

The 24-year-old Denmark international made 12 appearances for Chelsea last season and wants regular first team football.

On my Edson! Ajax want West Ham's Alvarez back

Ajax are trying to re-sign West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez.

The Dutch side sold Alvarez to West Ham for £35million in 2023 and now hope to buy him back.

West Ham want around £12.5m but Ajax sources say they are still owed money from the way payment was structured on the original transfer.

The 28-year-old, who has spoken to Ajax director Jordi Cruyff, spent last season on loan at Fenerbahce and was part of Mexico's World Cup squad but has generally struggled to live up to expectations since leaving Amsterdam.

Real Sociedad are also interested in Alvarez but are proposing a smaller, structured deal.

Edson Alvarez in action for Mexico against England at the World Cup

Rock on Tommi to Meadow Lane

Aston Villa winger Tommi O'Reilly is in talks to join League One Notts County on loan.

The 22-year-old had been set to sign for Sheffield Wednesday but, after further discussions, Villa have decided Meadow Lane may suit his development better.

O'Reilly had an outstanding campaign with Crewe last season and Villa hope he can replicate that form under Notts County coach Martin Paterson.

Notts County also signed Australian forward Luka Smyth from Finnish top-flight side VPS yesterday for an undisclosed fee on a three-year deal.

Notts County are in talks over a deal for Villa's Tommi O'Reilly

Perri set for Italian job after Trafford deal

Leeds United goalkeeper Lucas Perri is expected to join Torino on loan with an option to buy once a deal for James Trafford is completed.

Trafford, 23, is poised to sign a deal worth around £130,000 a week once Manchester City and Leeds finalise details on an expected £40m transfer with £5m in add-ons and a sell-on clause.

Torino and Leeds have agreed an initial loan move for Perri for the coming season. The deal also includes an option to buy him permanently next summer.

Leeds goalkeepers Karl Darlow and Illan Meslier have left Daniel Farke’s squad to join Manchester United and Arsenal this summer.

They would still like another as cover as well as strengthening at left-back, attacking midfield and striker.

Lucas Perri's Torino deal may be signed off after James Trafford arrives from Manchester City

MONDAY: Leeds close in on deal for James Trafford

SUNDAY: Liverpool seek compromise on Bradley Barcola

SATURDAY: Tottenham continue push for Man City winger Savinho

FRIDAY: Real open talks for Yan Diomande, Chelsea go back to Villa to poach set-piece coach Austin MacPhee... and Brentford bid for West Ham wing back

THURSDAY: Arsenal sign Christos Tzolis in £34million move from Club Brugge as Leeds ramp up talks with Man City's James Trafford

WEDNESDAY: West Ham star Crysencio Summerville set for £60m Saudi Arabia move despite Roma's late attempt to hijack deal

Sports.title: Real Madrid to hold contract talks with Arsenal target Vinicius Jr as transfer saga takes a new twist: Club expect Brazilian star to STAY despite stand-off as Jose Mourinho makes stance clear
Sports.content:
Real Madrid will hold talks with the agents of Vinicius Jr this week as they try to find common ground on a new contract.

Arsenal remain attentive to developments after posting their interest in the potential blockbuster signing of the 26-year-old should the opportunity arise for what they recognise would be an expensive transaction.
