Mourinho faced media on Tuesday as Madrid ran out 4-1 winners in a friendly over Leganes, but there were no bold statements as the Spanish media expect the club to keep one of their prized assets.

Madrid and his representatives are due to meet this week with the intention of making progress on a new long-term deal.

Mourinho has telephoned Vini Jr and is understood to have told him he wants him to stay.

Real Madrid are set to hold contract talks with Vinicius Jr, with Arsenal still interested

Madrid are still in the throes of agreeing a fee with RB Leipzig for winger Yan Diomande but the Ivory Coast international is set on moving to Santiago Bernabeu.

Some Arsenal insiders fear their efforts are futile but others want to continue to press in case Madrid fail to reach an agreement.

Meanwhile, Newcastle maintain they have still to receive a formal offer from Arsenal for Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal have been preparing an offer around £70million for Vinicius Jr's compatriot but proposals have come through his agent so far.

Newcastle maintain he is not for sale but manager Eddie Howe admitted last weekend he was unsure where his captain's future lies.

Sports.title: VOICE OF THE PADDOCK: I have proof Mercedes really are giving Kimi Antonelli special treatment over George Russell - and this is how Russell should respond
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton’s turnaround has been the most remarkable driver transformation of the year. Barely able to locate the right pedal last year, he has once again demonstrated reserves of resilience as deep as the Mariana Trench.

Nobody doubted him more publicly than himself, suggesting Ferrari should replace him. Nor did anyone hold him to higher standards than a certain Mr L Hamilton. It was always thus and an essential ingredient of his sustained success.

This year’s Ferrari suits him better than the 2025 edition, partly a product of getting himself more integrated into the team, which being Italian has a rhythm different from anything he experienced at either McLaren or Mercedes. This amalgamation is not about chumminess but getting the people – and by close extension the car – to work to his specifications.

There is also the Kim Kardashian factor. Has his relationship with the American media celebrity pepped up his fraying psyche, one wonders?

With these elements lined up, including his new race engineer Carlo Santi operating with him on the same wavelength, Hamilton is Kimi Antonelli’s closest and most realistic challenger, though 50 points back.

Yet…

Lewis Hamilton's turnaround has been remarkable - has his relationship with Kim Kardashian given him a new lease of life, one wonders?

Lewis has not 100 per cent returned to his soaring best. Niggling mistakes have cost him penalties four times in three races. Nor are Ferrari always 100 per cent slick in their strategy calls, plus ca change.

Hats off to Lewis, but there remains room for improvement. If you think the assessment is harsh, ask the perfectionist himself.

The scope of Antonelli’s rounded talent has slightly surprised me. His speed was never in question. But he was somewhat error-prone last year. It seemed he had been exposed to the trials of Formula One scrutiny too early, aged 18. He probably was.

But he has found his feet and is making statement drives most weekends, and often aggregating damage-limitation points when he is not quite sending fireworks into the sky.

I point to the moment it all changed for his title chances. It was when George Russell suffered technical problems in qualifying in China. Antonelli took pole and won the race. It was the sliding door Russell would have loved to have shut in his rival’s face. And look where each stands now.

You think Mercedes want Russell to win as much as they are rooting for Antonelli? I’ll tell you how I know they do not.

Last week in this column I wrote that Silver Arrows bigwigs were slightly and subtly, perhaps even unwittingly, pulling for the teenage Italian rather than for Russell. Kimi is their pet project, the one individual who fills the emotional gap left by Hamilton decamping to Ferrari to ask of the gods his destiny.

How did Mercedes respond to the observation I made seven days ago? There came not a word of protest. This would not be especially telling if it were not for the fact that in the days when Lewis was their hero, this kind of commentary would have been met with a swift retort by a Mercedes spokesperson via WhatsApp or phone. The absence of this admonition tells its own story.

Kimi Antonelli is Mercedes' golden boy. In truth, the scope of his rounded talent has slightly surprised me

You think Mercedes want Russell to win as much as they are rooting for Antonelli? I have evidence they do not

If I were Russell, I would be doing two things. The first, obviously, is to try to win the title despite the headwind blowing against him. The second, I would look to explore the possibility of moving teams for next season to start afresh.

If he does lose out on the title, Antonelli’s favoured status would be set in stone. He would be cast for eternity as a useful No2, a latter-day David Coulthard to Mika Hakkinen.

Saudi Arabian GP in Austria? Don't rule it out...

Imola is pencilled in to stage the final race of the season should Qatar and Abu Dhabi, still scheduled as the concluding rounds of the championship, follow Bahrain and Saudi Arabia as F1 casualties of war.

The biggest worry is whether the weather will hold in Italy. A finale in Europe on the last weekend of November carries some jeopardy, though it is worth a go and would be a fitting venue if either Antonelli of Italy, or Hamilton of the Scuderia, were to contest the title there, or indeed use Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari as a lap of honour.

The notion of Silverstone to celebrate Russell’s possible championship crowning? It doesn’t appear to be at the top of anyone’s to-do list. (Passim…)

Malaysia steps in to house the ‘Bahrain Grand Prix’. Held over from April, it is confirmed to take place on October 4, between the Azerbaijan and Singapore races.

Where will this transfer of one country’s race being held in another country end? I could see Bahrain’s neighbours in the Middle East region not wishing to miss out on the PR and therefore following the precedent somewhere else in Europe. The ‘Saudi Arabian GP’ home from home in Austria, perhaps. And so on.

Is this kind of relocation without precedent in sport? Royal Ascot at York in 2005 is the closest analogy that springs to mind. A personal moan, in passing: Ascot need never have moved had they not built those ghastly escalators in that overgrown stand of theirs. Christian Horner and I agree on this.

Lando Norris was superb in Hungary last weekend - do not rule him out for the world championship just yet

Write off Lando at your peril

A fine drive by Lando Norris at the weekend to win in Hungary, his second corner blip excepted. He cashed in on his luck when his team-mate Oscar Piastri was bizarrely delayed by backmarker Carlos Sainz, but he was mighty quick all afternoon in a promisingly upgraded McLaren.

Can Norris now push his nose into the championship fight? Well, 91 points is a big hurdle to jump. But possible with 11 of 22 or 23 rounds completed.

‘I’ll have some time away with my friends and family,’ said Norris ahead of F1’s summer holidays. ‘And play a bit of golf and padel, and try to lose a bit of weight.’

Fat-faced (ha!) or Slim Jim, he can at least enjoy being the pursuer, and relish being freed from the need to strive desperately for the first title he won last year. He may find it fun this time. Do not rule our Champ out yet.

Sports.title: Banned Olympian vanishes before 28th birthday as heartbroken mother makes desperate plea for help
Sports.content:
Banned Olympian vanishes before 28th birthday as heartbroken mother makes desperate plea for help

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The family of a former Brazilian Olympian is asking for help after the long distance runner disappeared from their home.

Daniel Nascimento, a marathoner who competed at the delayed Tokyo Olympics in 2021, left his home in a suburb of Sao Paulo on June 19 and has not returned since, according to an Instagram post from his mother.

The post - which his mother, Valdirene de Paula Ferreira, posted on Monday - asked for information regarding his whereabouts.

'His name is Daniel Nascimento. Better known [by the nickname] Armero,' she wrote in Portuguese.

'He was a marathon runner (he presents [with] psychological issues).'

According to Ferreira, her son left home in Paraguacu Paulista around 7:00pm on June 19 with a black backpack.

Brazilian marathoner Daniel Nascimento has disappeared, according to his mother

Nascimento (L) was living at home after being banned from competing for five years after testing positive for multiple forms of steroids before the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris

Nascimento's best achievement was a third-place finish in the 2022 Seoul Marathon. He also briefly led the New York City Marathon (above) that same year before he collapsed in the heat.

He had been under her care after he was banned from competition for five years beginning in May 2025, according to The Sun.

The family only formally reported his disappearance to the authorities on Monday - the day before Nascimento's 28th birthday.

Ferreira pleaded for any helpful information, and even listed her phone number to her followers and beyond.

'I would go to work and he would come with me. He was always a good boy,' she reportedly said. 'Sometimes I used to take him out for a run.

'He would do some training sessions in secret in the middle of the sugarcane fields. I think he really missed the routine of being an athlete.

'A thousand things go through your mind as a mother. I think I've lost about 10 kilos. Daniel's siblings are also very worried. We just want him to show up.'

Nascimento is the fastest marathoner in South America, but was banned for competing for five years after he tested positive for three different steroids a month before the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris. The ban took him out of those games as well as the upcoming Los Angeles Olympics in 2028.

His biggest accomplishment was finishing third in the 2022 Seoul Marathon, running a 2:04:51. That year, he also led the New York City Marathon for over 20 miles before collapsing due to exhaustion on a hot race day.

Sports.title: Village cricket rocked by cheating allegation after Saltburn's clash with Norton
Sports.content:
Village cricket rocked by cheating allegation after Saltburn's clash with Norton

An investigation has now been launched into Saltburn’s 2nd XI cricket match with Norton in Division Two of the North Yorkshire and South Durham League

View 2 Images A village cricket game is being investigated

Village cricket has been rocked by a cheating scandal after a fielder was accused of clicking his fingers to mimic the sound of the ball hitting the bat.

‌



Footage appears to show a slip fielder for Saltburn 2nd XI snapping his fingers just before his wicketkeeper takes a catch. The batter appears confused to be given out.

‌



After the clip circulated, people accused him of fooling the umpire into thinking the batter had edged the ball.

‌



Ben Mummery, who shared the footage on social media, said: "Click-gate has gone viral and I’m genuinely really happy it’s being exposed. Harshest possible punishment please. It’s not cricket."

England cricket icon says wife was left 'suicidal' over Azeem Rafiq racism storm READ MORE :

View 2 Images An investigation has been launched into Saltburn’s match with Norton after cheating allegations (Image: Saltburn CC)

‌



The incident happened in a match in the North Yorkshire and South Durham League (NYSDL) between Saltburn 2nd XI and Norton 2nd XI, while ­Saltburn were fielding.

League leaders Saltburn ended up winning by a huge margin of 159 runs at their home ground in North Yorkshire.

Rory Cotterill, who captained Middlesbrough CC’s 2nd XI in a 29-run defeat to Saltburn in June, has since claimed a similar situation occurred in that match. He shared a video online which allegedly showed the same player clicking his fingers.

Article continues below

The NYSDL confirmed it received a formal complaint regarding S­aturday’s game.

It said: “A full investigation has been initiated and until such time as the formal processes are complete no further comment will be made.”

Saltburn CC has been approached for comment.

Sports.title: Glorious Goodwood tips: Wednesday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy
Sports.content:
Glorious Goodwood tips: Wednesday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy

Unmissable in-depth analysis of all eight races on the second day of the Festival which stages the week's signature race, the Sussex Stakes

View 6 Images Newsboy provides tips for Goodwood (Image: PA)

1.50 Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap: CANNES is entitled to a plea of mitigation following his Royal Ascot blowout and deserves another chance.

‌



A debut second to his stablemate James J Braddock at the Curragh last November, the son of Sea The Stars took the silver medal home from his return to action at Leopardstown in April, but went one better in handsome style at the Foxrock venue the following month.

‌



Joseph O’Brien then gave Cannes his handicap debut in the King George V Stakes punters bought into the plan - my selection went off the 7-2 market leader in a field of 19.

‌



Eastender Kaiya Fraser hoping to star on the big stage at Goodwood READ MORE :

His supporters were left out of pocket when Dylan Browne McMonagle’s mount returned in 14th place behind his Ryan Moore-partnered stablemate Enceladus - but there are excuses.

Despite the big field, the leaders didn’t go off at a breakneck pace and the race unfolded to favour those positioned nearer the front than the back, which is where Cannes found himself during the early stages.

The handicapper has left Cannes on an unchanged mark of 95 and that’s a rating that looks within range for a colt who has plenty more to offer, while the unstoppable form of his trainer’s team is another reason to be cheerful.

‌



Of the remainder, Hatteen , Infraad and, at bigger odds, Parisian Scholar are three-year-olds open to further progress who have a role to play.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 CANNES, 2 HATTEEN, 3 PARISIAN SCHOLAR

View 6 Images Karl Burke: trains Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

‌



2.25 British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes: WILD BLOSSOM is a two-year-old filly of significant promise who should make full use of this drop in class.

The daughter of Mehmas - dam Duchess Rose didn’t win but is a half-sister to Queen Elizabeth II Stakes hero Bayside Boy - cost 300,000 guineas at the breeze-up sales in April before being sent to join Karl Burke by owners Wathnan Racing.

Making her racecourse debut in a four-runner novice stakes for fillies over five furlongs at Carlisle the following month, Wild Blossom could hardly have been more impressive, sent to the front by James Doyle inside the two-furlong pole before careering away to humble Crownbreaker by 10 lengths.

‌



Sent off at 7-1 for the Group 2 Queen Mary Stakes at Royal Ascot, my selection completed in 10th, beaten just over four lengths, behind winner Victorious, with four of today’s opponents in behind.

But that effort merits an upgrade as subsequent events at the meeting showed the far side, where Wild Blossom finished third in a group of 11, was at a disadvantage to the stands’ rail. With her sights lowered to conditions-stakes level, Wild Blossom is expected to get back to winning ways before returning to Group company.

Fast Track, 14th in the Queen Mary before a runaway success at Beverley, is a strong candidate for the podium, along with Weatherbys Super Sprint winner Zigazig Ah and Hidden Gift.

‌



NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 WILD BLOSSOM, 2 FAST TRACK, 3 HIDDEN GIFT

View 6 Images Simon Crisford: trains Newsboy's pick with son Ed

5.00 Rolls-Royce Oak Tree Stakes - ZANTHOS hasn’t yet reproduced the form of her two-year-old season - but there’s no time like the present.

‌



Roll the clock back to the autumn of 2025 and the daughter of Sioux Nation, trained in tandem by Simon and Ed Crisford, was proving herself in a higher grade than the company she’s keeping today.

A debut winner at Newmarket in August, Zanthos was unexpectedly beaten at odds of 4-11 at Leicester a month later. But she left that form well behind when outpointing The Prettiest Star by half a length for the Group 2 Rockfel Stakes back at Newmarket on her final start as a juvenile. It’s no calumny against Zanthos to say things haven’t worked out so far this term.

Returning in Longchamp’s Poule d’Essai des Pouliches in May, Oisín Murphy’s partner finished ninth of 15 behind Diamond Necklace and, stepping back from a mile to six furlongs, she came back 16th of 22 in the Group 1 Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot won by Venetian Sun.

‌



But seven furlongs on fast ground are the conditions that have shown Zanthos, fitted with a tongue strap, in her best light and the drop to Group 3 level will help her bid to bounce back. Flora Of Bermuda carries a penalty for her success in York’s Group 3 Summer Stakes 19 days ago but is feared most, ahead of Planet Seeker and Radiant Beauty.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ZANTHOS, 2 FLORA OF BERMUDA, 3 PLANET SEEKER

View 6 Images Kaiya Fraser: won on Adonius at Chester (Image: PA)

‌



3.35 Veuve Clicquot Molecomb Stakes: ADONIUS is the choice to give Co Durham trainer Rebecca Menzies a winner at Goodwood with her first-ever runner at the track.

The son of Soldier’s Call is already the best horse dual-purpose trainer Menzies has handled on the Flat - and is still a long way from the bottom of the barrel.

Reputed to be full of spirit during his pre-training days, Adonius was gelded prior to his debut at Musselburgh at the beginning of April but channelled his energies in the right direction to score by seven lengths.

‌



Adonius had just a neck to spare over Rlasthope under a penalty in East Lothian eight days later but did enough to earn a trip to Chester’s May fixture, where he contested the curtain-raising Lily Agnes EBF Conditions Stakes.

Again in front from flagfall under Kaiya Fraser, my selection took his record to 3-3 with a length-and-a-quarter dismissal of Hickory Lad.

Menzies resisted the temptation to go to Royal Ascot with Adonius, whose train-to-catch way of doing things will be well suited to the South Downs as he moves up to Group 3 level, and her patience can yield its reward.

‌



Pershaada, Ruler’s Pride and El Floridita were all beaten in different races at the royal meeting but warrant respect, all the same.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ADONIUS, 2 PERSHAADA, 3 EL FLORIDITA

View 6 Images Bow Echo (right) wins by a short head from Gstaad (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

‌



4.10 Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes: BOW ECHO has yet to taste defeat and is expected to take the score in his private battle with Gstaad to 3-0.

A perfect 3-3 as a two-year-old - he won a Newbury maiden, Haydock Park’s Listed Ascendant Stakes and the Group 2 Royal Lodge Stakes at Newmarket - the Night Of Thunder colt went into his winter quarters as one of the leading candidates for the 2,000 Guineas.

Bow Echo was an uneasy 9-2 chance on the big day, despite one upbeat bulletin after another from trainer George Boughey in the lead-up to the Rowley Mile test on the first Saturday in May.

‌



In the event, Billy Loughnane’s partner defied the market drift, coming from the back of the field to lead at the furlong pole and holding Gstaad by two and three-quarter lengths at the line, the pair a whopping eight lengths clear of third home Distant Storm.

Bow Echo went off at 5-6 to confirm that superiority over his Aidan O’Brien-trained rival in the St James’s Palace Stakes and did so - but only by a short head.

The result suggests that the momentum is with Gstaad, but Bow Echo tended to over-race after being leant on by the runner-up leaving the stalls yet demonstrated another facet to his game in being able to win ugly.

‌



It’s not hard to share Boughey’s view that Goodwood’s contours will play to Bow Echo’s strengths and he receives the vote to remain unbeaten.

Ten Bob Tony and Opera Ballo, first and third in the Queen Anne Stakes at the royal meeting, are taken to duke it out for the final place on the podium with the returning Zavateri and the top-class if quirky Never So Brave.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 BOW ECHO, 2 GSTAAD, 3 OPERA BALLO

‌

5.00 Coral Charlton Handicap: UNDER THE TWILIGHT was narrowly denied at this meeting 12 months ago but compensation is at hand.

The Michael Blake-trained mare went under by a neck to Dubai Treasure in the handicap for fillies and mares over course and distance, having scored at Windsor on her previous start. Under The Twilight then met with defeat on her next 10 starts but was back in business on Thameside 16 days ago.

‌



Sent off at 6-1 in a field of 12, Harry Davies’ mount came from the rear of the field to beat Amazonian Dream, who went one better at the track a week later, by a length and a half.

That success was gained from a British Horseracing Authority rating of 73 and Under The Twilight is 5lb higher in the handicap today.

But even that revised figure of 78 is 4lb beneath the mark from which she suffered last year’s near-miss, so the weights and measures point to another bold show.

‌



In a wide-open affair, Velvet Rhythm, French Affair, Lipsink and Calling A Star just four horses who merit a second glance.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 UNDER THE TWILIGHT, 2 VELVET RHYTHM, 3 CALLING A STAR

View 6 Images James Owen (second right) trains Newsboy's pick (Image: PA)

‌



5.40 HKJC World Pool Handicap: GOLDMOYNE has been a gold mine for punters since joining James Owen and another good run is on the cards.

The ex-Irish six-year-old son of Galileo Gold has won six of his 19 outings for the Newmarket trainer, the most recent success coming on Polytrack at Lingfield Park in March.

Goldmoyne has made the frame in five of his seven races since then, but that doesn’t mean the British Horseracing Authority handicapper has caught up.

‌



Two starts ago, my selection ran down the centre of the course to finish second to Royal Zabeel at Newmarket, where the winner was favoured by being stationed towards the far side. And his third, beaten two heads, behind Northern Express at York 19 days ago was another fine effort against a course specialist who was cashing in on a falling mark.

Hardly a day goes by without Owen saddling a winner, and jockey Mason Paetel’s 5lb claim is another plus. Bobby Bennu, Crimson Spirit and Zarathos are at the top of a long shortlist.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 GOLDMOYNE, 2 BOBBY BENNU, 3 ZARATHOS

Sports.title: Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Goodwood on Wednesday on ITV
Sports.content:
Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Goodwood on Wednesday on ITV

The in-form tipster hopes to continue his run of winning selections on day two of Glorious Goodwood when he has three tips including Ban Royale in the opener

View Image Steve Jones with his picks for Glorious Goodwood on ITV

Make it pay with Bay on day two of Glorious Goodwood. BAY ROYALE (1.50) has shown heaps of promise in three novice and maiden races. He now makes his handicap debut and he looks to have been handed an attractive weight.

‌



It’s hard to understand how he is priced up at much bigger odds than both Hatteen and Infraad, considering he was much too good for both rivals on his return to action at Nottingham in May.

‌



He couldn’t quite follow up under a penalty when runner-up – again at Nottingham – but he bumped into smart prospect Knights Charge and the front pair were well clear of the rest.

‌



Eastender Kaiya Fraser hoping to star on the big stage at Goodwood READ MORE :

A two-month break since that run should have done him some good and Harry Eustace’s well-bred three-year-old should enjoy the step up to 1m4f for the first time. Have 1pt each-way at 10-1.

ARDUIS INVICTA (5.00) is fairly unexposed over 6f and this speed-favouring course should play to her strengths. She was placed at Listed level as a juvenile last autumn and she has been holding her form this season.

‌



After finishing runner-up over 5f at Musselburgh, she put in another decent performance, despite finding herself short of room at a crucial stage, when fourth at York last month. She looks capable of going close. Have 1pt each-way at 40-1. A few bookies are paying out on six places.

DEFENCE MINISTER (5.40) hasn’t had much luck with the draw in two starts since making a winning return on Kempton’s all-weather track in March. He had little chance racing out of stall one on the far side in the Victoria Cup at Ascot in May in a race dominated by horses that raced towards the stands’ side.

Article continues below

It was a similar story in the Buckingham Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot when he used up a lot of energy to cross towards the favoured nearside from another unhelpful stall. He didn’t have the greatest draw in the race 12 months ago but it didn’t stop him finishing an excellent fourth in a race where the form worked out really well.

This year’s race doesn’t look as strong and, although the luck of the draw has deserted him once again, it’s not impossible to get a decent early position from his stall 13. If he does finally get the rub of the green, he should be very competitive. Have 1pt each-way at 25-1. Most firms are offering five places.

Sports.title: Loose horse causes Goodwood Cup chaos after getting in way in ‘important part of race’
Sports.content:
Loose horse causes Goodwood Cup chaos after getting in way in ‘important part of race’

Trawlerman was practically stopped in his tracks by the riderless Amiloc in the straight before Scandinavia completed an impressive victory in the Group 1

View 2 Images Scandinavia chases the loose Amiloc at Goodwood (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

A loose horse caused chaos in the £500,000 Goodwood Cup after getting in the way ‘in the most important part of the race’ on Tuesday.

‌



The 2m Group 1 was supposed to produce a rematch between Ascot Gold Cup first and second, Scandinavia and Trawlerman, the horse who trains in special goggles to protect his eyes from the sun.

‌



Yet there was drama from the outset as first Trawlerman anticipated the start to burst out of the gate half a length in front of the rest. Then Amiloc lost his rider Hector Crouch who, after a valiant effort to stay in the saddle, was dumped on the turf.

‌



The riderless Amiloc decided to race ahead of the field, with Trawlerman kept a safe distance back leading the rest of the field.

But as soon as William Buick launched his bid for victory, Amiloc came right across the front of him, forcing the jockey to take evasive action to avoid a collision. With momentum lost, Scandinavia forged clear to win by eight and a half lengths.

Describing the interference afterwards, Buick said: “It’s significant. It’s hard to say how significant. He got in the way in the most important part of the race. It definitely had an effect.”

‌



View 2 Images Hector Crouch goes off the side of Amiloc (circled) as Trawlerman (far side) steals an advantage (Image: ITV)

Trainer John Gosden said: “When you’ve been crossed like that and checked, he’s not the type to turn around and start quickening. We got the worst of it and we went from being a length and a half in front to a length and a half behind. That’s racing.”

The stewards report said: “Approximately 2 furlongs out, the riderless AMILOC edged right-handed towards the rail resulting in the rider of TRAWLERMAN (IRE) having to take a check for a number of strides when placed on the heels of AMILOC, but after viewing a recording of the incident, it was found that no riding offence was involved.”

‌



After looking into the incidents at the start the stewards were satisfied that Amiloc was a runner “as the rider was mounted as the start was effected before AMILOC jumped left-handed, resulting in Crouch catching his leg on the starting stalls, causing him to become unbalanced and ultimately unseated shortly after the start.”

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The report added: “TRAWLERMAN (IRE), drawn 8, anticipated the start and accelerated the gate at the same moment as the start had been effected, thereby enabling the gelding to break quickly. Being satisfied that it was not caused through a faulty action of the starting stalls, no further action was taken.”

Article continues below

Scandinavia’s jockey Ryan Moore said: “He couldn’t have done anymore than what he done today. I never asked him for everything.”

Sports.title: UEFA hit back at FIFA plan to SELL World Cup in bitter war of words
Sports.content:
UEFA hit back at FIFA plan to SELL World Cup in bitter war of words

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is reportedly planning to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors but European football’s governing body have fired back at that plot

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino faced severe criticism throughout the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

UEFA have taken aim at FIFA and said that football is ‘not theirs to sell’ in the face of their outrageous plan. Recent reports have suggested that world football’s governing body is planning on selling stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

‌



The scheme could see FIFA president Gianni Infantino earn millions if a deal is rubber-stamped. The administration of US President Donald Trump has reportedly been consulted.

‌



And while the plan is still being mulled over by those within the organisation, it has not gone down well within UEFA.

‌



A statement from the Champions League organisers on Tuesday afternoon read: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross.

Roberto Mancini named new Italy manager as Claudio Ranieri makes shock return READ MORE :

“UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.”

‌



FIFA have already explained their plan in detail. In a statement, they confirmed that FIFA intends to expand football development funding to over $10 billion (£7.49 billion). That funding would then be available to all 211 associations that are members of FIFA.

View 2 Images Trump's administration have already been told about FIFA's plan (Image: Getty Images)

FIFA would remain as majority stakeholders in the World Cup, with private investors buying 20 to 30 per cent, and the member organisations would receive a small stake totalling 20 per cent.

‌



The Times has reported that one senior figure within the game has labelled FIFA’s plan as a "nuclear bomb" for the game.

FIFA President Infantino has regularly courted controversy this summer, particularly when it comes to the World Cup. Supporters took aim at him for the sky-high ticket prices during the tournament.

He was also criticised for his role in the decision to reverse Folarin Balogun’s ban for a red card. The American forward was initially suspended after being sent off, only for that decision to be reversed following a phone call from US President Trump.

Article continues below

On the criticism he faced, Infantino said : “You were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all. To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at Fifa are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering ‌the best show in the ‌world. We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100% safety and security, only joy and happiness.”

Sports.title: Man Utd learn Iliman Ndiaye asking price in transfer battle for Everton star
Sports.content:
Man Utd learn Iliman Ndiaye asking price in transfer battle for Everton star

Manchester United are considering a move for Iliman Ndiaye, who also has interest from Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal, but Everton are set to ask for a hefty transfer fee

View 2 Images Iliman Ndiaye is in demand (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

Everton will demand around £70million for in-demand star Iliman Ndiaye amid interest from Manchester United and Al-Hilal. Ndiaye, 26, is a wanted man after a couple of eye-catching seasons on Merseyside.

‌



The forward is open to leaving Everton and his camp would encourage a bid from the Saudi Arabian side. But United are also in the running, with left wing among their priorities this summer.

‌



Michael Carrick's side have shortlisted Ndiaye and are tracking his situation. The Athletic report that Everton are aware of Al-Hilal's interest, although no talks between clubs have taken place.

‌



It's added that Everton are expected to ask for a fee similar to the £70million that Barcelona paid Newcastle United this summer for Anthony Gordon. Ndiaye also has three years left on his contract and the Toffees are in no rush to sell him.

However, their search for a left winger isn't as pressing as other areas, with Marcus Rashford due to be integrated back into the squad after a season on loan at Barcelona.

‌



There have been claims that Everton would like to hand Ndiaye an improved contract in order to fend off interest, but he's rejected their proposals. The Toffees paid £15m for Ndiaye two years ago when he arrived from French giants Marseille.

The former Sheffield United star has scored 17 goals and provided three assists in 71 appearances for Everton. Ndiaye went to the World Cup with Senegal, starting one of their four games as they reached the last 32.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua team member slams Simon Jordan after wild conspiracy theory
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua team member slams Simon Jordan after wild conspiracy theory

Anthony Joshua was dropped twice in the opening round by Kristian Prenga on Saturday night, but rallied to a stunning second round knockout in Saudi Arabia

View Image Anthony Joshua knocked out Kristian Prenga (Image: Getty Images)

A member of Anthony Joshua's team has brutally hit back at Simon Jordan after the talkSPORT presenter questioned the Brit's knockout victory over Kristian Prenga.

‌



'AJ' returned to the ring on Saturday night for the first time since being involved in a tragic car crash over in Nigeria which resulted in the deaths of close friends Latif Ayodele and Sina Ghami.

‌



The former two-time heavyweight champion was dropped twice in the opening round by the Albanian, but sensationally rallied to a second round knockout victory. Joshua's remarkable win has guaranteed a date with long-time rival Tyson Fury - which is due to take place before the end of the year.

‌



Yet Jordan was rather sceptical of the end result, writing: “Not having that … #anthonyjoshua fight. Dropped twice and sets the tempo, how’s that ? … Prenga totally different in 2nd. Something not quite right , all designed to rinse maximum amount of money …”

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Jake Paul and Eddie Hearn team up in shock move to end heated rivalry READ MORE :

Sergey Lapin, Director of Team Usyk, has since brutally hit back at Jordan's remarks. Joshua teamed up with the Ukrainian's team prior to his bout with YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul back in December - and Lapin once again played a key role on Saturday night.

In an interview with Action Network, Lapin said: "What do I think of Simon Jordan’s comments? I suppose they also told Prenga to walk straight into a punch that weighed one and a half tonnes. Everyone is entitled to their own theories. I have a friend who still believes the Earth is flat and that space doesn’t exist. Personally, I’d rather discuss what actually happened inside the ring than someone else’s imagination."

Kristian Prenga's team addresses conspiracy theories after Anthony Joshua loss READ MORE :

Lapin was quick to turn his attentions to Joshua versus Fury, and is confident his man can secure a devastating knockout over the 'Gypsy King.' "Time certainly plays a role. It helps you recover, refine your game, and sharpen your timing. But time alone doesn’t win great fights," he said.

Article continues below

"When it comes to Joshua versus Fury, I genuinely believe AJ can knock Tyson Fury out. This is the kind of fight where one mistake changes everything. Both men have what I call a “red button”—one decisive shot capable of ending the night. The question isn’t whether the fight happens in one month or six. The question is who finds that moment first. That’s why I believe AJ can finish the fight inside the distance."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.
